new_quiz.q: What is a notify in an animation?
choices: A marker on the animation timeline that sends an event when the animation reaches it
A message in the Output Log that reports an animation error
A setting that makes an animation loop without end
A bone that other bones are attached to on the skeleton
new_quiz.explain: A notify sits at one moment on the timeline. When playback reaches it, it sends an event, so something in the world can happen at exactly that moment.

new_quiz.q: Which node plays AM_Interact on the character in this quest?
choices: Play Sound at Location
Set Actor Transform
Play Montage
Add to Viewport
new_quiz.explain: Play Montage starts the montage and has outputs such as On Completed, On Interrupted and On Notify Begin that tell you what happened.

new_quiz.q: The Play Montage node runs, but the character does not play the animation. What do you check first?
choices: That the lever has a Niagara effect
That the Slot of the montage exists in the AnimGraph of the character
That the montage has more than two sections
That the trigger volume is larger than the lever
new_quiz.explain: A montage plays through a named Slot, such as FullBody or UpperBody. If the AnimGraph has no node for that Slot, the montage has no way into the final pose.

new_quiz.q: What do you use the On Completed output of Play Montage for?
choices: To spawn the effect on the hand
To start the montage again
To show the prompt on the screen
To unlock the player
new_quiz.explain: On Completed fires when the montage has played to its end. That is the moment to give control back to the player.

new_quiz.q: What should happen when a hit or a jump interrupts the montage?
choices: The lever stays half pulled for the rest of the game
The montage stops and the actor goes back to its starting state
The montage plays again from the Reach section
The character is destroyed and spawned again
new_quiz.explain: On Interrupted is where you cancel the interaction cleanly. The lever or chest returns to its starting state, so the player can try again.

new_quiz.q: At which moment of the montage do you place the notify for the effect?
choices: At the moment when the hand touches the object
At the first frame of the montage
At the last frame of the montage
At the moment when the player presses the key
new_quiz.explain: The effect must match what the viewer sees. Placed on the contact frame, the sound or the Niagara effect appears exactly when the hand reaches the object.

new_quiz.q: Where is the Niagara effect or the sound spawned when the contact notify fires?
choices: At the Player Start of the level
At the center of the trigger volume
At a socket on the hand
At the position of the camera
new_quiz.explain: A socket is a named point on the skeleton. Spawning at a socket on the hand puts the effect where the contact happens.

new_quiz.q: What do you use the On Notify Begin output of Play Montage for in this quest?
choices: To unlock the player after the montage
To cancel the interaction
To create the montage sections
To change the state of the lever or chest
new_quiz.explain: The second notify fires On Notify Begin in the Play Montage node. Your graph uses it to change the state of the actor at the right moment of the animation.

new_quiz.q: What does the master sequence LS_First need on its Shots track?
choices: One shot that is 15 seconds long, with no camera
At least 2 shots, each with its own Cine Camera
At least 5 shots that share one camera
Only audio clips and no shots
new_quiz.explain: A master sequence is built from shots. Here it has at least 2 shots, and each shot has its own Cine Camera.

new_quiz.q: What is the Camera Cuts track for?
choices: It makes the master sequence cut between the cameras
It trims the animation clip of the character
It deletes cameras that are not used
It renders the sequence to image files
new_quiz.explain: The Camera Cuts track decides which camera the viewer looks through at each moment. You place the cut at a clear moment in the action.

new_quiz.q: The walk animation of the character is longer than the shot. What do you do with the clip?
choices: Delete the character from the shot
Make the master sequence longer than 15 seconds
Blend or trim the clip so that it fits the shot
Move the clip to the Camera Cuts track
new_quiz.explain: An Animation clip on the track can be trimmed and blended. You fit the clip to the shot, and the length of the sequence stays as planned.

new_quiz.q: In the Level Blueprint, what do you call when the player enters the Box Trigger?
choices: Go to End and then Stop
Create Widget and then Add to Viewport
Open Level and then Play
Set Playback Position with the value 0 and then Play
new_quiz.explain: Set Playback Position with 0 moves the sequence to its first frame. Play then starts it, so it always runs from the beginning.

new_quiz.q: How does the F key skip the sequence?
choices: It calls Go to End and Stop
It calls Set Playback Position with the value 0
It closes the Level Blueprint
It removes the Camera Cuts track
new_quiz.explain: Go to End jumps to the last frame, and Stop ends the playback. The level is then in the state it has after the cinematic.

new_quiz.q: Where do you open Movie Render Queue?
choices: In Edit, then Editor Preferences, then Keyboard Shortcuts
In the Show menu of the viewport
In Window, then Cinematics, then Movie Render Queue
In the Place Actors panel, under Cinematic
new_quiz.explain: Movie Render Queue is in the Cinematics group of the Window menu. It needs the Movie Render Pipeline plugin to be enabled.

new_quiz.q: Movie Render Queue is missing from the menu. What do you check first?
choices: That the sequence has a Camera Cuts track
That the Movie Render Pipeline plugin is enabled
That the level has a Box Trigger
That the project was packaged
new_quiz.explain: Movie Render Queue comes from the Movie Render Pipeline plugin. Without the plugin, the menu entry does not exist.

new_quiz.q: You render with a .png Sequence [8bit] export. What do you get in the output folder?
choices: One video file for the whole sequence
One PNG file for each shot
One text file with the camera settings
One PNG file for each frame of the sequence
new_quiz.explain: An image sequence saves every frame as its own file. The folder with the numbered PNG files is part of your proof.

new_quiz.q: What is a core loop?
choices: A Timeline that plays without end
The first level of a game
The short cycle of actions that the player repeats
The event that runs on every frame
new_quiz.explain: The core loop is what the player does again and again: reach a goal, face a threat, get a reward, and win or lose.

new_quiz.q: Which five things do you write down for your loop?
choices: The goal, the threat, the reward, the fail state and the win state
The level, the light, the sound, the camera and the menu
The mesh, the material, the texture, the rig and the animation
The title, the genre, the price, the platform and the date
new_quiz.explain: These five lines describe the whole loop. If one of them is missing, the game has no tension or no end.

new_quiz.q: How does damage lower health in this quest?
choices: The Data Table lowers the health on every frame
The widget lowers the health when it is drawn
The Game Mode lowers the health of all actors each second
Apply Damage sends the damage, and Event AnyDamage on the hit actor lowers its health
new_quiz.explain: Apply Damage only sends an amount of damage to an actor. That actor reacts in Event AnyDamage, where both the player and the enemy lower their Health.

new_quiz.q: How do the Blueprints get their tuning numbers?
choices: They read the numbers from the HUD
They read the rows of DT_Tuning with Get Data Table Row on Begin Play
They ask the player to type the numbers
They copy the numbers from the Output Log
new_quiz.explain: DT_Tuning holds values such as player Health and enemy Speed. Get Data Table Row reads a row, and the Blueprint stores the values when the game starts.

new_quiz.q: Why do you not type tuning numbers directly into the graphs?
choices: Numbers in a graph are not saved
Numbers in a graph slow down the game
You can then tune the game from one table
Graphs can only hold whole numbers
new_quiz.explain: With all numbers in one table, tuning is fast and safe. You change a row, play again, and compare how the game feels.

new_quiz.q: How do you mark the enemies so that your logic can recognize them?
choices: Give them Gameplay Tags that start with Character.Enemy and check with a Has Tag node
Give them a red material and check the color
Place them in a folder named Enemy in the Outliner
Make their names longer than the name of the player
new_quiz.explain: A Gameplay Tag is a label with levels, such as Character.Enemy. A Has Tag node tests for the label, so the logic does not depend on a class or a name.

new_quiz.q: When does BP_CoreGameMode show WIN?
choices: When the player Health <= 0
When the score reaches the target
When the first enemy is spawned
When the restart input is pressed
new_quiz.explain: The Game Mode keeps track of the score and the lives. It shows WIN when the score reaches the target, and LOSE when the player Health <= 0.

new_quiz.q: What does WBP_HUD show, and where is it added to the viewport?
choices: The frame rate and the memory, added from the Game Mode
The enemy Speed and enemy Damage, added from the Data Table
The names of all actors, added from the Level Blueprint
Health, Score and the score needed to win, added from the Player Controller
new_quiz.explain: The HUD shows the numbers the player needs to follow the loop. The Player Controller creates the widget and adds it to the viewport.

new_quiz.q: What is a master material?
choices: A material that only one prop may use
One material with many parameters, from which artists make Material Instances
A material that is made by the engine for each level
A folder that holds all the materials of a project
new_quiz.explain: A master material leaves values open as parameters. Artists get different looks from instances and do not have to build new materials.

new_quiz.q: What does MPC stand for?
choices: Material Parameter Collection
Mesh Preview Camera
Master Prop Class
Material Property Copy
new_quiz.explain: MPC is short for Material Parameter Collection. It is an asset that stores parameters which many materials can read.

new_quiz.q: What is a User parameter on a Niagara system, such as SpawnRate or TintColor?
choices: A note for the artist that has no effect
A setting that only works in the editor preview
A password that locks the system
A value of the system that can be set from outside, for example by a Blueprint
new_quiz.explain: A User parameter is exposed on the system. A Blueprint can change it during play, and the effect reacts.

new_quiz.q: With which prefixes do the names of the Material Instances and of the Niagara system start?
choices: M_ and BP_
T_ and SM_
MI_ and FXS_
MPC_ and L_
new_quiz.explain: Material Instances start with MI_ and the Niagara system starts with FXS_. The prefix tells the kind of asset from the name alone.

new_quiz.q: What must the Blueprint with the BP_ prefix do?
choices: Change the value of the effect during play
Create the master material when the game starts
Rename the instances in the Content Browser
Delete the effect after one second
new_quiz.explain: The Blueprint changes the value while the game runs, started by a key press, a trigger or a timer. This shows that gameplay can control the effect.

new_quiz.q: If you drive the effect from an MPC value, what else should that same value change?
choices: The size of the level
The names of the Material Instances
The frame rate of the game
M_Master_Prop, so that the props and the effect react together
new_quiz.explain: Materials can read a Material Parameter Collection too. One value then changes the props and the effect at the same moment.

new_quiz.q: What does your usage note for artists list?
choices: The time you spent on each asset
Each parameter, its safe range, and which Blueprint call drives the effect
The engine version and the installed plugins
The meshes of the scene and their triangle counts
new_quiz.explain: The note tells artists what they can change, how far they can go, and how the effect is driven. They can then use your work without asking you.

new_quiz.q: Why do you give the parameters groups and names that artists will understand?
choices: So the material compiles faster
So the Niagara system can read them
So artists can find and use them in an instance without opening the graph
So the parameters cannot be changed by mistake
new_quiz.explain: Artists work in the Material Instance, where they only see the parameter list. Clear names and groups make that list easy to use.
